subject.title: fix(discord): sustained gateway bursts stop growing memory

question: Should Discord Gateway overload deliberately reject additional non-critical sends after one queued 120-event window instead of retaining stale work indefinitely?
rationale: The patch prevents unbounded memory growth, but it intentionally changes overload behavior for ordinary Gateway operations and needs maintainer acceptance of that delivery-versus-bounded-memory tradeoff.

options.title: Accept the bounded rejection contract
options.body: Merge the owner-local queue cap because the documented 120-event window, caller containment, and loopback proof show bounded overload behavior without changing critical sends.

options.title: Require a different overload policy
options.body: Pause for a maintainer-defined coalescing or per-operation policy if ordinary Gateway sends must not reject under sustained backlog.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded rejection contract
recommendation.body: Merge the owner-local queue cap because the documented 120-event window, caller containment, and loopback proof show bounded overload behavior without changing critical sends.
